# Pixels & Paychecks: A Solo Dev's $20K Launch Week, Wishlist Math, and the Indie Stack

This week we crunch real revenue numbers from a one-person Steam debut, surface the wishlist-to-sales conversion every solo dev underestimates, and round up the communities and tutorial libraries quietly powering the next wave of hobby-to-shipping pipelines.

## Core Defense: Anatomy of a $20,186 Launch Week
Solo dev Mario Kaiser shipped Core Defense on Steam and banked $20,186 in week one — modest by triple-A standards, but a useful data point for anyone building small. Months later, with zero Steam sales run, the title is already sitting at roughly 2.5x that first-week revenue, and an Android + iOS port is queued to stretch it further. The takeaway: a clean launch is a starting line, not a finish. [1]

## The Wishlist-to-Revenue Math Nobody Tells You
Kaiser leans on Simon Carless's research showing that first-week Steam revenue typically grows 2–5x over a game's first year as accumulated wishlists slowly convert to sales. Core Defense is out-performing that benchmark without a single discount — proof that the months-long wishlist build before launch is the real campaign. [1]

## Finding Your Missing Co-Founder: Work With Indies
Work With Indies is positioning itself as the indie-specific job board and Discord hub that mainstream gaming-recruitment sites don't serve. Listings start at $49, the Discord runs resume and portfolio reviews, and the team has flagged an active scam impersonating the brand — a useful reminder that indie hiring culture is still maturing alongside the tooling. [3]

## From Hobby Project to Shipped Game: IndieGameDev's Tutorial Stack
IndieGameDev.net quietly maintains one of the better learning libraries aimed at hobby developers crossing into shippable territory: hands-on deep dives into rendering and engine architecture, a full OpenAL + C++ audio series, simple game-music production tutorials, and even a random game-idea generator for the moments when the blank page wins. [5]

## Sources
- [1] How to Make a Somewhat Successful Indie Game — https://frgmnts.blog/f/how-make-successful-indie-game.html
- [3] Work With Indies - Make Games, Together — https://www.workwithindies.com/
- [5] IndieGameDev | Solo, Hobby, and Indie Developers — https://indiegamedev.net/
